subject: URGENT: Geo surge causing P99 spikes on long-context (32k) Hosted API
messages:
From: Alex Tanner <alex.tanner@brightgate.com>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: support@brightgate.com
Date: 2026-11-12T08:14:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Production — P99 degradation for long-context requests

Hi Karthik,

We started seeing a sharp increase in P99 latency around 07:50 PST across multiple regions (primarily us-west). The affected requests are mostly our batch inference jobs and interactive sessions that use the 32k window — p99 jumped from ~400ms to 3.2s and error rate climbed ~1.8%. This is killing our SLA for proactive routing.

I've attached a small sample of requests and a log bundle. Can you confirm whether this is a deployment change on the Hosted API side or an underlying node/network congestion? We had no config changes on our end.

We need immediate assistance — these are production traffic spikes and our customers are seeing timeouts.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Tanner
Head of Platform Engineering, BrightGate
Attachment: brightgate_p99_sample_requests_20261112.json (json)
Attachment: svc_logs_20261112_geo_node_bundle.zip (zip)
From: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Tanner <alex.tanner@brightgate.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-12T08:28:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Production — P99 degradation for long-context requests

Alex — thanks for flagging and for the artifacts. I've ingested the request samples and forwarded the bundle to infra. Initial checks: no planned deploys in the 07:30–08:00 window; routing controls show a geo burst to us-west.

Immediate next steps I am kicking off now:
- Marcus (infra) to triage host-level metrics and kernel/quantization fallbacks for long-window work.
- Rishi (runtime) to confirm if padding/batching behavior regressed for 32k paths.
- I'll open an incident and loop in on-call to get a mitigation plan (rate-limiting, fallback to 16k model variant if needed).

Can you tell us: what fraction of these requests are low-entropy (prefix-heavy) vs unique customer prompts? That helps with caching/kv-hit analysis.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
From: marcus.lin@redwood.ai <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, alex.tanner@brightgate.com
Date: 2026-11-12T09:01:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Production — P99 degradation for long-context requests

Following up with the initial triage:
- Node metrics: increased CPU scheduling delays and nvlink saturation on a subset of us-west nodes between 07:45–08:10.
- Kernel selection: runtime fell back to a slower attention kernel on ~18% of 32k requests caused by a memory alignment pattern we haven't hit in prod at scale.
- Autoscaling: scaling events were delayed by ~45s due to load spikes; control plane rate limiter prevented immediate burst capacity.

Mitigation applied at 08:55: temporarily routed new 32k requests to secondary pool in us-east and enabled a conservative batching cap (max in-flight tokens) for us-west. Early numbers show p99 trending down but still elevated.

I'll attach a short log excerpt in the incident ticket.

-Marcus
From: laura.bennett@redwood.ai <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: alex.tanner@brightgate.com
Date: 2026-11-12T10:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Production — P99 degradation for long-context requests

Thanks team. Alex — I'm looping in a couple of exec-level watchers to make sure BrightGate has visibility while we work mitigation and a post-incident plan.

Immediate asks for the incident update:
- Marcus: ETA on full traffic rebalancing across regions and whether we can auto-failover 32k heavy tenants to alternate pools without requiring customer opt-in.
- Rishi: root cause hypothesis for the attention-kernel fallback + whether a temporary model-variant (16k trimmed) can be served with comparable quality.
- Karthik: prepare an external status note for BrightGate's ops channel summarizing impact and immediate mitigations (short, <5 bullets).

Laura Bennett
VP, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
From: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai
Cc: alex.tanner@brightgate.com
Date: 2026-11-12T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Production — P99 degradation for long-context requests

Prelim technical notes:
- The long-context (32k) execution path hit an edge where KV cache alignment plus certain attention mask shapes forced a non-optimized kernel (higher memory copies and serialized attention). This shows up when prompt tokens include many small segments and heavy metadata embeddings — matches BrightGate samples.
- Temporary options: 1) soft-fallback to 16k-quantized variant with prefix expansion (quality delta ~1.5% for their workload), 2) enable aggressive prefix caching if identifiable prefixes exist, 3) throttle concurrency for 32k requests per-tenant to protect tail latency.

I recommend pursuing (1) as a short-term protective measure while Marcus finishes traffic rebalancing. We'll instrument a canary for correctness drift.

-Rishi
From: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: alex.tanner@brightgate.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-12T16:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Production — P99 degradation for long-context requests

Alex — quick status update for your ops channel (short note you can paste):

1) Impact: Intermittent P99 spikes and a small rise in 5xxs for BrightGate long-context (32k) requests affecting ~8% of produced traffic between 07:45–09:00 PST.
2) Root cause (initial): kernel fallback + nvlink congestion on a subset of us-west nodes triggered by geo burst of long-window traffic.
3) Mitigation in place: rerouted new 32k traffic to us-east pool, applied conservative batching cap in us-west, enabled tenant-level throttles for long-window concurrency.
4) Next steps: (a) will canary a 16k trimmed model-variant for BrightGate (quality check), (b) infra will rebalance and add autoscale buffer, (c) post-incident RCA and perf regression test scheduled.
5) ETA for full recovery: monitoring indicates rolling normalization over next 2–4 hours; we will confirm when P99 stable under target.

Attachments: incident ticket and log bundle submitted to your team. Please let us know if you need escalation to an incident bridge — we can open one now.

-Karthik
